newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Truck seizures halt Hungarocamion Russia supplies.
newsitem.headline: Truck seizures halt Hungarocamion Russia supplies.

text.p: Central Europe's largest road haulage company Hungarocamion said on Friday it had halted deliveries to Russia following the seizure by Russian customs of five trucks worth 125 million forints ($750,000).
A company spokesman said customs officials in the Russian province of Bryansk had refused to allow the five trucks to leave, saying they did not have papers proving tax had been paid.
"We have no choice," the spokesman Gyorgy Rozsa told Reuters. "We have 11 trucks there but the authorities told five of the drivers to go home and leave their trucks behind."
Rozsa said the drivers had refused to leave the lorries and would stay until the problem was resolved.
Hungarocamion carries up to half of all Hungary's road exports to Russia, while the former Soviet Union accounts for 15 percent of the company's annual turnover of 20 billion forints.

Rozsa said the customs officers in the Russian regions of Kursk and Bryansk had temporarily seized 25 Hungarocamion trucks with correct documents in the first eight months of the year, claiming that duties had not been paid on the goods transported.

Hungarocamion's managing director Gabriella Szakall earlier told Hungarian news agency MTI that Russian customs officers commonly harassed drivers of Hungarian and Western trucks without apparent justification.
She said Russia had joined the TIR international transport agreement but had neglected to adjust internal regulations.
"Administration procedures are slow and inaccurate, and practices are of a protectionist nature are employed to the detriment of foreign transporters," she said.
She said Hungarocamion will enlist the help of Hungary's foreign and trade ministries to release the impounded trucks.

Hungarocamion is due to be privatised next year. The state privatisation agency APV said on Tuesday it would sell an 80 percent stake in the company Hungarocamion, which has registered capital of 5.23 billion forints.
